bull_bear.body: Priority 1: Core business (India/Africa network); Priority 2: Deleveraging (Net Debt/EBITDA 1.1x); Priority 3: Adjacencies (DC, FinServ, Cloud); Dividend hiked 50% to Rs.24/share; Africa stake acquisition via non-cash share swap with ICIL; No major non-India acquisitions planned outside bolt-ons.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Geopolitical crisis impacting international roaming and capex (INR depreciation); Supply chain constraints (memory/chipset) affecting Homes business; Energy price volatility; Handset price inflation potentially slowing smartphone upgrades; Regulatory execution on NBFC.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident on structural ARPU upside ('pricing architecture is broken'), disciplined on capital allocation, aggressive on adjacencies (DC/FinServ), transparent on short-term roaming headwinds but long-term optimistic.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Management explicitly stated Indian unlimited data pricing (Rs.340-350 cap) is fundamentally broken compared to global peers ($60-70), implying strong rationale for future tariff hikes even without cost pressure; Nxtra's Google partnership is a colocation model for AI data centers in Visakhapatnam, not GPU rental; AI now contributes 30% of all code written at Airtel.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Second-largest mobile operator globally by customer base, with nearly 666 million customers and networks covering over two billion people.
- India's largest integrated communications solutions provider with a diversified portfolio spanning mobility, broadband, enterprise, and digital services.
- Strong brand and distribution reach, evidenced by 4% revenue market share improvement over the last 5 years and a record 4.2 million net additions in Homes Broadband in FY26.
- Vertically integrated digital infrastructure including India's largest data centre network (Nxtra) and passive infrastructure via Indus Tower, supporting enterprise and digital growth.
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Network quality, expansion and transformation — Identified as a material topic; failure to maintain and expand network quality could erode competitive positioning and customer experience.
- Information security and customer data privacy — Material topic reflecting the critical need to protect customer data and maintain trust in an increasingly digital operating environment.
- Regulatory compliance — Material topic given the highly regulated telecom sector; non-compliance could lead to penalties, operational restrictions, or reputational damage.
- Climate change, energy efficiency and emission reduction — Material topic as energy-intensive operations face transition risks and physical risks, impacting cost structure and long-term sustainability.
- Talent attraction and human capital development — Material risk related to the ability to attract, develop, and retain skilled talent necessary for innovation and operational execution.
- Sustainable supply chain management — Material risk involving supplier compliance with health, safety, and working condition standards, with potential for operational and reputational impact.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body: Bharti Airtel provides high-speed 4G/5G mobile, Wi-Fi (FTTH and FWA), digital TV, and digital payments to retail consumers, while offering enterprises secure connectivity, cloud and data center services, cyber security, IoT, and cloud-based communication. The company operates in 15 countries across India and Africa, with additional presence in Bangladesh and Sri Lanka through associate entities, and its digital arm Xtelify empowers global telcos with AI-driven digital transformation.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Consumer Mobility:** 4G/5G mobile services
- **Homes Broadband:** FTTH, FWA, Digital TV, IPTV
- **Enterprise Solutions:** Secure connectivity, Cloud and data center services, Cyber security, IoT, CPaaS, SD-WAN
- **Digital Services:** Airtel Finance, Airtel Payments Bank, Xtelify (AI platform for telcos), Airtel Cloud (sovereign cloud platform)
- **Passive Infrastructure:** Indus Tower Limited (tower infrastructure)
business.title: Products & brands

business.body: - Nxtra by Airtel — subsidiary: Operates India's largest network of 14 hyperscale/core facilities and 120+ edge data centres; data centre business scaling capacity from ~250 MW to One GW over the next few years.
business.title: Group structure (profile)

business.body:
- Second-largest mobile operator globally by customer base, with nearly 666 million customers and networks covering over two billion people.
- India's largest integrated communications solutions provider with a diversified portfolio spanning mobility, broadband, enterprise, and digital services.
- Strong brand and distribution reach, evidenced by 4% revenue market share improvement over the last 5 years and a record 4.2 million net additions in Homes Broadband in FY26.
- Vertically integrated digital infrastructure including India's largest data centre network (Nxtra) and passive infrastructure via Indus Tower, supporting enterprise and digital growth.
business.title: Competitive strengths

latest_quarter.body: EBITDAaL margin improved 20bps QoQ to 52% (India ex-passive); Cost headwinds from server/memory prices and energy (diesel transition to solar/renewables); 'War on waste' initiatives mitigating opex/capex inflation; 42,000 sites now solar-enabled.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: Strong underlying growth in Africa (1.1% constant currency) and India; Margin: Targeting sustained >51% EBITDAaL via 'war on waste'; Order Inflow: B2B funnel healthy with multiple large enterprise wins; Capex: India core radio capex moderating, transport/fiber doubling down; FY27 capex expected 'in the ballpark of this year' (Rs.31k Cr India ex-passive base).
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: B2B order book grew 17% in FY26; secured 24 Airtel Cloud deals in FY26 with further wins in April; Nxtra building 56 edge data centers over next 18-24 months; Monthly loan disbursement run rate >Rs.550 Cr.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Data Centers: Targeting 1GW capacity, raised $1B fund for Nxtra; Financial Services: NBFC license received, Payments Bank revenue run rate Rs.3,400 Cr (+23% YoY); Cloud: Sovereign cloud traction with 24 deals; Africa: 16.3% stake increase approved, leveraging low tele-density (45%) and smartphone penetration (52%).
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Invest in future-ready digital infrastructure across core businesses, digital portfolio, and emerging growth engines, including ongoing 5G expansion and accelerated fiber deployment.
- Build a diversified digital services portfolio across Cloud, Cybersecurity, IoT, CPaaS, Financial Services, and data centres to deliver unified connectivity and bundled solutions.
- Enhance customer proposition through simplified offerings, seamless omnichannel journeys, and continuous digital innovation, leveraging home-grown digital tools and platforms.
- Leverage AI at scale for enterprise-wide transformation, customer experience enhancement, and operational excellence.
- Embed 'War on Waste' (WoW) deeply into operations through disciplined execution, digital interventions, and process simplification to reset costs.
- The Dividend Distribution Policy ensures a consistent approach to the Company's dividend payout plans and outlines the key parameters to be considered for dividend distribution.
- Occupational Health and Safety Management System (OHSMS) certified under ISO 45001, driven through the 'Airtel Suraksha' initiative with dedicated Health & Safety Committees at central and circle levels.
- Lost Time Injury Frequency Rate (LTIFR) for employees increased to 0.64 per million person-hours worked in FY 2025-26 from 0.40 in FY 2024-25.
- 94.83% of value chain partners (by value of business) assessed on health and safety practices and working conditions.
- AirtelShield mobile and web app enables anonymous reporting of hazards, near-misses, and safety violations, with a strict non-retaliation policy and stop-work authority for all workers.
- Supplier Safety Policy and Consequence Management Matrix govern value chain partner compliance, with enhanced onsite audits and safety trainings implemented during the year.
- Transition assistance programme 'Limitless Horizons' provides a three-month retirement support programme covering purpose discovery, well-being, emotional resilience, financial security, and post-retirement planning.
- Sustainable Procurement Policy covers organisational governance, human rights, labour practices, environment, fair operating practices, consumer issues, and community involvement and development.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Airtel continues to invest in building future-ready digital infrastructure across its core businesses, digital portfolio and emerging growth engines. Ongoing 5G expansion and accelerated fiber deployment are aligned to meet rising data demand and evolving customer requirements. The data centre business continues to scale, with plans to significantly expand capacity in line with rising demand for data localisation and digital infrastructure.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Demand for high-speed, reliable connectivity accelerating across consumers and enterprises, driven by growing smartphone penetration and increasing demand for home connectivity.
- Data consumption continues to rise, supported by 5G investments enhancing network capacity and expanding addressable market through FWA and enterprise use cases.
- Data centre business scaling with plans to significantly expand capacity in line with rising demand for data localisation and digital infrastructure.
- Strengthening cloud capabilities, including launch of private cloud offerings for enterprise customers.
- India's digital economy and telecom sector acting as foundational infrastructure for digital transformation, with deepening digital inclusion strengthening economic multiplier.
- Rising cross-border data flows, expansion of Global Capability Centres, and increasing digital adoption supporting growth in technology-driven services and digital trade.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Airtel delivered record consolidated revenue (Rs.2.11L Cr) and EBITDAaL margins (51.2%) in FY26, driven by India mobile premiumization and Homes expansion, while strategically pivoting capital toward high-growth adjacencies (Data Centers, NBFC, Cloud) and consolidating Africa stake via share swap. The key inflection point is the management's explicit admission that Indian pricing architecture is 'broken,' signaling imminent tariff hikes to unlock ARPU beyond the Rs.257 Q4 level despite short-term roaming headwinds.
